svg.text: Registry rules from primary sources and registry code, verified 14 Oct 2026 · not part of the trust score · snapshot 13 Oct 2026, 09:14 UTC

g.text: Owned namespacesCan a publisher own a name prefix that nobody else can publish into?
Confusable names blockedDoes registration reject a name confusable with an existing package?
Uploads scannedAre new uploads analysed for malware automatically, by the registry or a feed it acts on?
Withdraw, keep lockfilesCan a version be withdrawn from new resolution while existing lockfiles still install it (yank)?
Deletion restrictedAre authors prevented from deleting a published version after the fact?
Client acts on advisoriesDoes the default client warn about or block known-vulnerable versions without extra tools?

rect.title: PyPI · Owned namespaces: no. One flat namespace. Namespace prefixes (PEP 752) are accepted but not deployed.
PyPI · Confusable names blocked: partial. A new name is rejected if it matches any existing project after removing . _ - and folding l/i→1 and o→0 (ultranormalize). Other misspellings pass.

PyPI · Uploads scanned: partial. Report-driven: trusted researchers (Observers) report through an API, and admins quarantine projects (hidden from the index, frozen) pending review. Auto-quarantine is proposed.
PyPI · Withdraw, keep lockfiles: yes. Yank (PEP 592): resolvers skip the release unless it is pinned exactly.
PyPI · Deletion restricted: no. Owners can delete files and releases at any time; only the filename can never be reused.
PyPI · Client acts on advisories: no. pip does not check advisories; pip-audit is separate.
npm · Owned namespaces: partial. @scope/ names belong to a user or organisation, but scopes are optional and unscoped names are first come, first served.
npm · Confusable names blocked: partial. A new name is rejected if it equals an existing one once punctuation is removed (2017). Other misspellings pass.
npm · Uploads scanned: partial. Malicious packages are removed and replaced by a '0.0.1-security' holding package, but npm does not document how they are detected.
npm · Withdraw, keep lockfiles: partial. npm deprecate only warns; the version still resolves. Hiding it means unpublishing, which also breaks lockfiles.
npm · Deletion restricted: yes. Unpublishing is allowed within 72 hours, or later only for packages with no dependents, under 300 weekly downloads and one owner.
npm · Client acts on advisories: partial. npm install runs an audit by default and reports known vulnerabilities, but installs them.
crates.io · Owned namespaces: no. One flat namespace. Namespaced crates (RFC 3243) are accepted but not implemented on crates.io.

crates.io · Confusable names blocked: partial. - and _ are equivalent (canon_crate_name), so such variants cannot be registered. A typosquat check runs after publication and only emails the crates.io team.
crates.io · Uploads scanned: partial. Typosquat checks on new crates alert the team; malicious crates are deleted, their accounts disabled and a RustSec advisory published.
crates.io · Withdraw, keep lockfiles: yes. cargo yank: new resolution skips the version; Cargo.lock keeps using it.
crates.io · Deletion restricted: yes. Deletion is allowed within 72 hours, or later only for crates with one owner, no dependents and few downloads (RFC 3660).
crates.io · Client acts on advisories: no. Cargo does not check advisories; cargo-audit (RustSec) is separate.
RubyGems · Owned namespaces: no. One flat namespace; prefixes are a naming convention only.
RubyGems · Confusable names blocked: partial. A push is rejected if the name equals an established gem's (≥ 10,000 downloads or released in the last five years) ignoring case, _ and -.
RubyGems · Uploads scanned: yes. Every upload gets static and dynamic analysis and a risk score; high scores go to manual review. The team reports finding 70–80% of the malware it removes itself.
RubyGems · Withdraw, keep lockfiles: no. A yank removes the .gem file, so locked installs of it fail.
RubyGems · Deletion restricted: no. A yank, possible at any time, deletes the file; only the version number stays taken.
RubyGems · Client acts on advisories: no. Bundler does not check advisories; bundler-audit is separate.
Go · Owned namespaces: yes. The module path is a domain or repository path, so whoever controls the domain or repository controls the name.
Go · Confusable names blocked: n/a. Names are domains and repository paths; there is no registration step.
Go · Uploads scanned: no. The mirror caches whatever a VCS serves; malicious modules are removed on request.
Go · Withdraw, keep lockfiles: yes. A retract directive in a later go.mod hides the version from new resolution; go.mod requirements keep it.
Go · Deletion restricted: yes. The mirror and checksum database keep every version; deleting the tag upstream changes nothing.
Go · Client acts on advisories: no. The go command does not check advisories; govulncheck is separate.
Maven Central · Owned namespaces: yes. A groupId must be verified before publishing: a DNS TXT record for the domain, or the code-hosting account for io.github.*.
Maven Central · Confusable names blocked: n/a. Names sit under a verified namespace, so confusable names fall under namespace verification.
Maven Central · Uploads scanned: no. Central validates signatures and metadata on upload but documents no malware analysis; malicious components are removed once reported.
Maven Central · Withdraw, keep lockfiles: no. Nothing can be withdrawn.
Maven Central · Deletion restricted: yes. Released components can never be changed or deleted.
Maven Central · Client acts on advisories: no. Maven does not check advisories; plugins such as OWASP Dependency-Check are separate.
Packagist · Owned namespaces: yes. A vendor prefix belongs to the first account to publish under it; nobody else can add packages to it.

Packagist · Confusable names blocked: partial. A package whose vendor is one edit away from an existing vendor with the same package name is rejected if the existing package has ≥ 1M downloads; otherwise the admins are emailed.
Packagist · Uploads scanned: yes (since Mar 2026). Aikido's malware detections are imported and shipped in the metadata Composer reads; Composer 2.10 blocks flagged versions.

Packagist · Withdraw, keep lockfiles: partial (since Jul 2026). Soft deletion removes a version from the metadata Composer resolves, keeps a record and can be undone; lockfiles fetch archives from the forge, which the maintainer controls.
Packagist · Deletion restricted: partial (since Jul 2026). Deletion is now a recoverable soft delete with a public record, but the code lives in the maintainer's repository, which they can delete.
Packagist · Client acts on advisories: yes. Composer blocks versions with security advisories during update/require by default (policy.advisories.block); installs from a lockfile are not checked.

svg.text: "since" marks a recent change. Hover a cell for the rule and its source; full notes and links in policies.md.
